candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — heparin adverse effects
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize local hematoma as a possible subcutaneous heparin effect while distinguishing it from clinically significant bleeding that requires evaluation.

options.A: Local irritation or hematoma can occur after subcutaneous heparin, but significant or worsening bleeding requires evaluation.
options.B: Any local hematoma proves the injection was administered incorrectly.
options.C: Injection-site hematoma is unrelated to heparin therapy.
options.D: Any small hematoma requires permanent discontinuation of heparin without further assessment.

candidate.rationale: Current heparin labeling lists local irritation, erythema, mild pain, hematoma, or ulceration as possible effects after deep subcutaneous injection. Because heparin also carries clinically important bleeding risks, significant or worsening bleeding findings require assessment rather than automatic reassurance or blanket discontinuation. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Local irritation and hematoma may follow deep subcutaneous heparin injection; bleeding remains a clinically important adverse effect requiring evaluation when significant.
candidate.source_locator: Adverse Reactions — Local Irritation; Warnings and Precautions — Hemorrhage
candidate.stem: A client receiving deep subcutaneous heparin develops a small localized hematoma at an injection site. Which interpretation is most accurate?
